clue.text: Very hot month — bother!

parts.note: FEB is the usual short form of February
to bother someone is to irk or rile them

explanation.surface: Someone sweltering in a heatwave month and cursing about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Febrile means feverish, so running a high temperature: very hot in the medical sense.

clue.text: Slip on yellow top that's soft

parts.note: a fluff is a slip or blunder, as when an actor fluffs a line

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: Pulling on a soft yellow top, like a cosy fleece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the slip above the Y in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Downy, fleecy things are soft to the touch, the sense of a cuddly toy.

clue.text: Sure to inhale dope, the mad dog

indicators.note: breathing something in takes it inside, so the other letters go into the word for sure

parts.note: bound, as in 'bound to happen', means sure or certain
a dope is a fool, an ass

indicators.note: mad signals that the letters of the word 'the' are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone certain to have smoked dope, the crazy dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sure' is the adjective in 'bound to win', not an agreement; 'mad' scrambles only the short word 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-legged, long-eared hunting breed is one particular kind of dog.

clue.text: Unite a trio of redheads, furious with enmity

indicators.note: furious suggests wild agitation, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the head of 'red' is R, and a trio of them gives three Rs

explanation.surface: A plea to reconcile three angry redheads who are at loggerheads.
explanation.definitionFit: Families or groups that marry into one another are united by those weddings.

clue.text: Follow leaders in extremely nail-biting situation, until exhausted

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters, so the first letter of each of the next five words is taken

explanation.surface: Advice to keep going through a tense, nail-biting moment until worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come after as a result, so to follow on.

clue.text: See 24
Europeans taking siestas up, one on deck doffing cap

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, i.e. backwards

parts.note: siestas are afternoon naps
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: doffing a cap removes the top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a deck is a pack of playing cards

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers napping, one of them stretched out on a ship's deck with hat off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NAPS into SPAN; 'doffing cap' turns CARDS into ARDS. 'Europeans' leans on the siesta stereotype.
explanation.definitionFit: People from Spain are one nationality of Europe, so they are Europeans.

clue.text: Top ten record astonishingly's beginning to climb

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the letters run upwards, so in reverse

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten
an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A record astonishingly climbing into the top ten of the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to climb' reads X, EP and A from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: An apex is the peak or summit, the highest point of something.

clue.text: 11 encapsulating old capital, but it's lacking for native American

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: the answer to 11 across is a stylised flower, an emblem based on the iris

indicators.note: the word 'it' is missing from the capital's name

parts.note: Quito is the capital of Ecuador

explanation.surface: A cross-reference clue that reads like a puzzle about a lost old capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The 11 answer is the heraldic lily, an emblem drawn from the iris flower; 'it's lacking' removes those two letters from the Ecuadorian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iroquois are a confederacy of indigenous peoples of north-eastern America.

clue.text: Gas ring not working, blocked by end of pipe

indicators.note: something blocked by an obstruction has it stuck inside
working here means being worked over, so the letters of the two words are rearranged
the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A gas ring that won't light because its pipe is blocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges RING NOT into NITROGN, and the E from 'end of pipe' sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen is a chemical element that is a colourless gas, most of the air we breathe.

clue.text: Happy band, unhappy

parts.note: up means cheerful, as in feeling up
a set is a band's performance, or a group

explanation.surface: A cheerful band turns into an unhappy one.
explanation.definitionFit: Being upset means being distressed or troubled, which is to be unhappy.

clue.text: Fall guy, git kidnapping primate, shot

indicators.note: a kidnapper holds the victim inside, so other letters go within

parts.note: 'git!' is slang for clear off, as is 'scat!'
an ape is a primate
a shot at something is a go

explanation.surface: A lout snatching a monkey and then shooting it, an absurd crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'git' looks like the insult, but here it is the American order to clear off; 'shot' means an attempt, not gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall guy is someone made to take the blame for others, which is just what a whipping boy does.

clue.text: Person about to accept Sumerian shop is a bloomer

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the other pieces go inside
about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: one's self is one's person
Ur was an ancient Sumerian city
a deli is a delicatessen, a kind of shop

explanation.surface: Someone about to let a Sumerian open a shop, which turns out to be a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns SELF into FLES. 'bloomer' looks like a mistake; it means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleur-de-lis is a stylised iris, so it is a flower, something that blooms.

clue.text: Cash for spending a penny, we hear? That's the game!

indicators.note: we hear means the words are taken as heard, not as written

parts.note: spending a penny is British slang for using the toilet, the loo, and cash is dough

explanation.surface: Money for a public toilet, and a cry of triumph at the end of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spending a penny' is British slang for going to the toilet, from the old coin-operated locks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludo is a board game of dice and counters, a children's favourite.

clue.text: Naval bruiser chewed thistle in a roll

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other

parts.note: a bap is a soft bread roll

indicators.note: chewed means mangled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A burly sailor chomping a thistle in a bread roll, an absurd sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a roll' is the British soft bread bun; 'chewed' scrambles the plant's letters before they go in.
explanation.definitionFit: A warship built for heavy fighting is a naval bruiser, a heavyweight of the fleet.

clue.text: A figure hugging tree then dull? Yes!

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping round, so other letters go inside

parts.note: five is a figure, a number
a fir is a tree
mat, or matt, means dull, without shine

explanation.surface: Asking whether a figure-hugging garment then looks dull, and answering yes.
explanation.definitionFit: An affirmative is an answer of agreement, the way yes is.

clue.text: Criminal, if loose, untreated?

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the first two letters of the word untreated, split off

explanation.surface: Asking whether a criminal on the loose has had no treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'untreated' splits: UN joins IF LOOSE as fodder and 'treated' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Felonious means relating to a felony, a serious crime, so it is criminal.

clue.text: Couple of idiots identifying the house sparrow?

parts.note: a twit is a fool
a twat is a vulgar word for a fool

explanation.surface: Two fools spotting a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Twit-twat is an old dialect name for the house sparrow, from its chirp.

clue.text: Ancient individual breaking leg

indicators.note: breaking into means getting inside, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: a leg of a journey is a stage
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: An old person breaking a leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stone Age is the prehistoric period, used of anything very old or primitive.

clue.text: Woman on the throne admitted to lowest act, unfortunately, in the smallest room

indicators.note: being admitted is being let in, so these letters go inside
unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen on the throne

explanation.surface: The Queen let into a low act, sitting on the throne in the smallest room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the throne' and 'smallest room' are both toilet slang; the Queen's throne is the real one. 'unfortunately' rearranges LOWEST ACT round ER.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest room is a British euphemism for the lavatory.

clue.text: Adjust fastener held by Greek character the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way means the whole is turned round and read backwards
held by means gripped inside, so one piece sits in the other

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a nut is a fastener for a bolt

explanation.surface: Fitting a fastener held by a Greek letter the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' places the fastener after the first letter of the Greek letter, and 'the wrong way' then reverses the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To attune an instrument or a mind is to adjust it into harmony.

clue.text: Look with you on land, might you say?

indicators.note: the answer with 'you' placed on it makes the land, so the U comes off the front
might you say means the words are taken as they sound

parts.note: Uganda is a country, a land
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: Taking a look at somebody's land with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you' (U) on top of the answer sounds like Uganda.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a gander is British slang for having a look.

clue.text: Somewhat discreet, in the shade

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone being discreet by staying in the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A tint is a shade or hue of a colour.

clue.text: While nowhere to be seen, I take seat in building

parts.note: to nab is to take or grab

indicators.note: building means constructing, so the letters are put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Unseen, I grab a seat inside a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' looks like the place but rearranges SEAT IN into SENTIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means while absent, as of a trial held without the defendant present.

clue.text: French port where British don't work

parts.note: to rest is to not work

explanation.surface: A French port where the British take it easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Brest is a major naval port in Brittany, north-western France.

clue.text: Pole in this building with Irish infestation?

definitions.text: Pole in this building with Irish infestation?

parts.words: Pole in this building with Irish infestation?
parts.note: firefighters slide down a pole in this building, and 'infestation' said with an Irish lilt sounds like it

explanation.surface: A Pole inside a building overrun with something Irish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person; it is the brass pole crews slide down.
explanation.definitionFit: The building housing engines and crew, with a pole for quick descent, is where firefighters wait.

clue.text: Guardian setter after a pay increase almost getting nothing — that's tedious!

indicators.note: after means the setter's piece is placed following the rest

parts.note: the newspaper speaks with an editorial 'we'

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a pay increase is a rise
O is the round figure for nothing
the setter of a crossword refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A Guardian setter grumbling that a pay rise has come to almost nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wearisome tires you out, which is exactly what tedious things do.

clue.text: See 2
The doctor of poetry, not entirely a classical hero

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Dr Seuss wrote rhyming children's verse

explanation.surface: A doctor of poetry being only partly a classical hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus, who slew the Minotaur, is a hero of Greek myth.

clue.text: Jumper with clothes for TV show

parts.note: a jumper, a British word for a sweater, is a top
gear is informal for clothes

explanation.surface: Wearing a jumper and other clothes for a television appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a pullover sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: Top Gear is a long-running BBC motoring television programme.
